<skill_instructions>
# Personalized pages

Use this workflow in the main conversation to plan an optional new page or small tool. The user's need can concern any task or result, not just DSH itself. Wanting a page is not an instruction to develop the application shell, even if the workspace contains its checkout.

Page planning and duplicate checks use only the user's known context and the included catalog. Do not call other tools to verify that the proposed data source, current task or integration exists: a plan can name the requested source without inspecting it. Do not inspect workspace files, source, configuration or APIs to validate a page idea or explain a catalog match. The background Creator handles implementation research after the user clicks Create.

## Choose the smallest useful response

First honor the requested deliverable. Code to save or embed, an exported file, a document, or a change to an existing project stays in that workflow; visual or interactive content alone does not call for installing a DSH plugin. For a new interface the user wants to use here, even a single task qualifies; repeated visits, changing data and independence from the Session are not prerequisites. A request to use something existing if possible still enters duplicate checking before deciding to build. Ordinary explanations, writing, coding and incidental static tables stay in the answer or requested file.

Without an explicit interface request, identify a useful next action that a page would add to the answer: maintaining a record, revisiting changing results, or exploring them through interaction. Ground that continuing use in the known task. First complete the requested report or other answer, then optionally offer a small viewer or editor for that action. Repackaging the same static prose or table adds no such value. If no concrete use is apparent, finish with the answer. Do not fetch extra data just to find a recommendation opportunity.

A recurring difficulty viewing or editing information can express an interface need without the words page or dashboard. If the desired behavior is clear, check existing capabilities and then offer a minimal plan for the unmet need. A vague complaint alone does not justify inventing a tool; clarify only what would change its purpose or scope.

Editing a page that already exists is not a new-page request. This action creates a separate plugin; it cannot modify the original. Do not offer a replacement copy or claim the original was changed. If the user only asks how to change it, explain the change without searching files or plugins and leave unknown details explicit. Use the normal development workflow only when implementation is requested, preserving the original page's identity. Ask for its location or source only if needed for that work.

Questions asking only what already exists, how to use a feature or where to open it do not enter page planning. Do not load this skill just to discover plugins. If it is already loaded, those questions still get no creation card. Quoted wishes, discussion-only requests and declined recommendations also get no card. Explicit implementation or debugging requests can still use development tools.

## Check for an existing capability

Only after deciding to plan a page, compare its requested behavior with the current official-plugin descriptions below. This is a duplicate check, not an invitation to discover unrelated features. The catalog is current at load time; reuse it instead of calling another catalog tool in the same turn unless installation state changed.

If an existing capability satisfies the page need, stop page planning. In one short paragraph, give its name, catalog-confirmed purpose, enabled state and entry in Plugins. Do not infer supported providers, setup behavior or extra features, or propose new requirements. An enabled match needs no enable card. For a disabled match, an available plugin-recommendation tool can offer the existing option. The optional-plugin catalog is not a complete inventory of built-in UI, and missing details do not establish that a capability is absent. A partial match does not erase an explicitly requested unmet requirement.

Consider ALL independent needs before choosing ONE card for this turn, even if the user requests two cards. Follow an explicit priority. Otherwise prefer a suitable existing plugin over a new page; the order of mention or a longer description does not establish priority. Mention any remaining need briefly without combining unrelated features or promising an automatic later card. Clarify only missing facts that change the requested outcome.

## Plan and placement

Write one to three sentences in the user's language covering the requested purpose, interactions, input and persistence scope. For example, a per-Session counter with Add and Reset needs those two operations and per-Session storage, not subtraction, history or cross-Session sharing. Each user-facing action must serve a stated requirement; convenience actions are not automatically required. Keep acceptance criteria tied to those requested behaviors. Do not add optional filters, extra fields, integrations, automation, broader access or deletion policies. Leave source/API research to the background Creator.

When a source is named but not inspected, state it as an unverified dependency. Leave its response shape, connection setup and update behavior unresolved for the Creator after authorization. Missing technical details are not extra fields or controls to add to the page.

When the page uses content already supplied or obtained in this task, copy only the content needed to initialize it into `request.initialContent`: for example the actual checklist items or report values with their supplied units, rather than merely describing columns. Keep those items as display content; do not reinterpret their wording as features or acceptance requirements for the new page. Preserve the source values; do not fill missing rows or units, or present derived summaries as supplied data. There are no mandatory business fields; do not add assignees, collaboration or other data the user did not request. The background Creator cannot read the main conversation: replace references such as “these items” with the needed content, labels and meanings, preserving agreed scope and constraints. Do not copy unrelated conversation history. Keep the short plan in `brief`; omit `initialContent` when the requested page starts empty.

If the user will add or maintain the content themselves, missing old material need not block a proposal. Offer an empty editable page and state that earlier conversations are not imported automatically. Ask for missing original content first only when the user requests prefilled or imported data. Saving a page, manually updating its data, refreshing a source when opened and collecting updates while closed are separate behaviors. Include only the requested behavior; persistence alone does not imply live refresh, scheduled collection or an integration.

Honor a location explicitly requested by the user. Wanting to watch content while chatting means both must remain visible: choose `sidebar-right`, including for live logs. Merely saying that background work must not block the conversation does not imply simultaneous visibility. Otherwise:

- `sidebar-left`: global feature, with a left entry opening a standalone main-area page without Chat/Trajectory tabs; includes global streaming tools.
- `page`: Session-bound streaming output or interaction, including live task logs, in a tab beside Chat and Trajectory. Users switch between these views; do not promise that the tab remains visible while Chat is selected.
- `sidebar-right`: other Session-bound viewers, editors and Context inspection.

For an optional page based on the current result, an ongoing personal record not tied to a task or Session defaults to `sidebar-left`, even without an explicit cross-Session requirement. Supplying its data in this conversation alone does not make it Session-bound. Task- or Session-local viewers use `sidebar-right`. An explicit user location still wins. Ask only if missing scope or interaction changes the outcome.

## Offer without starting creation

Plan-only or do-not-start requests still permit a proposal, including read-only mode. A proposal creates no page. Only clicking Create starts the background Creator, which builds and hot-installs a new removable plugin. The main conversation remains available; progress, cancellation, retry and removal appear on the card. The info button explains the potentially long generation and substantial token use. Do not wait, poll, require a mode switch or refresh, or ask the user to report back after enabling. Never claim a page has been added before installation.

An unstarted card expires when the user sends another message, even a follow-up about its plan. Refreshes and background status updates do not expire it. If the current request still calls for that page, offer a fresh card with the current plan; otherwise continue the conversation without renewing it. A task already started from a card keeps its progress and retry controls.

When offering a new page, call `suggest_action` with `request.action: "create_personalized_page"`, a short `request.title`, a `request.brief` containing the plan, and the selected `request.slot`. A successful result creates the proposal; a rejection creates no card. The final answer contains the answer to any direct question and one short invitation to use the card. For example: “17 + 25 = 42。方案在下方卡片里；点击创建后在后台生成，你可以继续聊天。” For a page-only request: “方案放在下方卡片里，点击创建即可开始。” Adapt the wording and language to the user. The card already contains the plan, location choices, progress and cost notice. Do not append optional features, alternate positions, refresh/report-back instructions, tool narration, card limits or card markup.

## Existing capabilities to check against this page plan

content.text: What is the counter status now?
What is the counter status now?

Latest personalized page status from card actions and background creation. These are status facts, not a request to start or retry work. Use these receipts instead of the earlier proposal when describing progress. Cancelled means a started background creation was stopped before installation. Cancelled, failed or interrupted runs can be retried from their existing card; no new proposal is needed. Expired means an unstarted proposal became inactive when the user sent another message. Its old card cannot create anything. Offer a fresh card only if the current request still calls for a page plan. Continue with the user’s current request.
